The same capture carries full 2 to 500 page matrices: the internal generic path converts 500 pages in 535.34 ms at 111.44 MB B/op, the public library PDF in 532.24 ms at 113.10 MB B/op, and the public image path encodes 500 tiles in 34.02 ms. The 2026-09-11 perf-time closure and perf-improve captures and the 2026-08-19 0.2.4 rows stay on the page, each labeled historical. The concurrent-layout prototype was rejected (5.4% paired gain against a 15% floor) and left unwired. Open the Benchmarks page for the visual comparison.

content.title: Historical: allocation targets met, time targets split across two labeled windows (2026-09-11)
content.body: The 2026-09-11 perf-time closure capture held every allocation target: 500-page B/op was 163.02 MB (warm matrix), 167.87 MB (standalone), and 169.65 MB (public library), 28.4% to 30.6% below the pre-time baselines and under the 234.92 MB ceiling. The 500-tile image time held at 44.27 ms. That window did not reproduce the phase-6 time: 733.48 ms matrix median and 695.42 ms standalone, with identical B/op. The phase-6 capture of the same production source measured 576.33 ms / 163,032,880 B, a 2.13x speedup that met the 615 ms stretch target, and the measured-lever floor (<= 830 ms) held. The 250-tile image median was 25.72 ms, 0.72 ms above the 25 ms line; the phase-5b raw samples measured 24.15 ms. The 2026-09-12 capture supersedes these times with 535.34 ms (internal) and 532.24 ms (public PDF) at 500 pages, at 111.44 MB and 113.10 MB B/op. Historical raw evidence: plans/0.2.6/perf-time/results/phase-7/final-capture.md.

content.title: Lossless PNGs about 50% larger, an intended trade
content.body: The 2026-09-12 image rows encode 250 tiles in 16.78 ms at 141,917 B and 500 tiles in 34.02 ms at 282,749 B; tile counts are the benchmark's requested output tiles, 1024 px wide. The filter-none level-2 streaming writer (internal/imageout/pngfast.go) replaced image/png adaptive filtering above the direct-raster threshold. PNG stays lossless, decoded pixels are bit-identical, and files stay far below the 32 MiB maxImageEncoded budget. The about 50% PNG growth and the 1.97x / 2.22x speedup against the pre-time baselines are historical readings from the 2026-09-11 perf-time capture: 94,352 to 141,917 bytes at 250 tiles and 188,268 to 282,749 bytes at 500 tiles.

content.title: Concurrent-layout prototype rejected, left unwired
content.body: The phase-6 prototype rendered independent top-level sections in parallel and merged deterministically. It passed the equivalence contract (op-for-op display lists, page counts, date-normalized PDF bytes, golden 65/65, flat B/op), but its best paired same-process gain was 5.4% (serial 596 ms versus 564 ms at W=2), below the required 15% floor. It was rejected for shipping, pipeline overlap was not attempted, and production stays serial. The prototype and its differential tests were deleted in the 0.2.6 cleanup (plans/0.2.6/ponytail/0.2.6-ponytail-audit.md); no production caller remains.

content.title: Generic CLI, not the island-era path
content.body: The 2026-09-12 CLI comparison rows are the generic convert path against wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6.1 with patched Qt; the gowk-only cli-rss table is the same binary measured without the comparison engine. The current in-process, public PDF, and public image rows come from the full ascending matrices in the 2026-09-12 capture, one fresh 1x process per round and the median of three rounds; B/op and allocs/op are the median-time sample's raw values, never averages. The 2-page B/op rows include the one-time default-font work (about 4.0 MB on the internal path), so they are not like-for-like with the 2026-08-19 multi-iteration matrix. CLI cells are the median of three timed process runs after one warmup. Peak RSS is /usr/bin/time %M and is never mixed with B/op. Do not compare these RSS numbers to older island-era CLI snapshots.

content.heading: Historical public library PDF vs wkhtmltopdf CLI (2026-08-19, indicative)
Historical in-process PDF vs wkhtmltopdf CLI (2026-08-19, indicative)
What the numbers mean
items: CLI comparison is process wall time plus peak RSS for freshly built gowkhtmltopdf versus the installed comparison tool. Puppeteer RSS is the peak process-tree reading for the Node driver plus headless Chrome, not a single-process /usr/bin/time %M value.

The current matrices come from the 2026-09-12 capture on the 0.2.6 working tree (VERSION 0.2.5), built with make build. CLI, WeasyPrint, and Puppeteer rows are the median of 3 timed runs after one warmup; internal, public PDF, and public image rows are one fresh 1x process per round, median of three rounds, with B/op and allocs/op taken from the median-time sample and never averaged.

The 2026-09-12 capture has gowkhtmltopdf faster and at lower peak RSS than wkhtmltopdf at every tested size, including 500 pages (79,296 KiB versus 123,076 KiB). The older reading that gowk RSS was higher from 100 pages on belongs to an earlier capture and is historical.

Historical: the 2026-09-11 perf-time closure window ran slower on wall time than the phase-6 capture 15 minutes earlier (733.48 ms versus 576.33 ms at 500 pages) with identical production source hashes and identical B/op. The 2.13x result is the phase-6 row; the closure rows are kept alongside it rather than replaced.

The image writer trades about 50% more lossless PNG bytes for roughly 2x faster encoding; decoded pixels and dimensions are unchanged. The current 2026-09-12 rows are 16.78 ms / 141,917 B at 250 tiles and 34.02 ms / 282,749 B at 500 tiles; tile counts are the benchmark's requested output tiles, 1024 px wide.
The concurrent-layout prototype (5.4% paired gain against a 15% floor) is rejected for shipping and has no production caller.

2-page B/op rows include the one-time default-font work (about 4.0 MB on the internal path) because each sample is a fresh 1x process. Do not compare them to the 2026-08-19 multi-iteration matrix without that caveat.

The public Go library rows call Document.WritePDF and ImageDocument.WriteImage directly. The 2-page public library PDF row is 5.75 ms against the 260 ms wkhtmltopdf CLI baseline in the 2026-09-12 capture, about 45x; the older approximately 20x landing claim is historical.

The report fixture is testdata/golden/benchmarks/templates/report.html.tmpl with 20 invoice rows per requested page. Page islands and their convert.NewBenchmarkPDFRequest opt-in were removed in the 0.2.6 cleanup; every row is a generic-path measurement.

Full matrices, historical snapshots, and raw rows live in testdata/golden/benchmarks/, documentation/benchmarks.md, documentation/performance.md, and the 2026-09-12 raw captures under plans/0.2.6/perf-review/results/2026-09-12/.
